title: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1 - Ethics & Professional Responsibilities - Conflict of Interest - Lender and Borrower
exam: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1
subject: Ethics & Professional Responsibilities
topic: Conflict of Interest - Lender and Borrower

questions.q: Two friends decide to enter into a private mortgage agreement. They approach a paralegal to draft the promissory note and represent both of them (the lender and the borrower) to save on legal fees. What should the paralegal do?
options: Accept the joint retainer without issue since they are friends.
Decline to act for both the lender and borrower as their interests are directly adverse, raising an unmanageable conflict of interest.
Represent the lender but give legal advice to the borrower informally.
Draft the agreement and charge them a single flat fee divided equally.
questions.explain: Rule 3.04 (Conflict of Interest). The interests of a lender and a borrower are fundamentally adverse (e.g., terms of default, interest rates). A practitioner is generally prohibited from acting for both sides of a lending transaction due to the high risk of conflict, and must recommend independent legal representation.
